BUS.G11.T1.ADAPT.A1.title: Adapting to environmental challenges
BUS.G11.T1.ADAPT.A1.description: How a business adapts to challenges of the three environments: information management, strategic responses, mergers/takeovers/alliances, organisation design and flexibility, social responsibility, and lobbying, networking and power relationships.
BUS.G11.T1.ADAPT.A1.strand: T1 — Business environments, socio-economic issues, sectors, ownership & acquiring a business
BUS.G11.T1.ADAPT.A1.recovery_strategy: Lobbying = influencing decision-makers. Networking = building useful contacts. Power relationships = strategic alliances and persuading big investors. Mergers/takeovers combine firms; flexibility and information management prepare the business for change it cannot control.

questions.question: When a business cannot control an environment, what is the realistic response?
questions.memo: A business cannot control the market or macro environment, so it must adapt — change its own plans to fit the new situation.

questions.question: When two businesses combine to form one, it is called a _________.
questions.memo: A merger is when two businesses join together to become a single, larger business.

questions.question: True or false: Lobbying is one way a business can respond to its macro environment.
questions.memo: Lobbying — influencing decision-makers and regulators — is a recognised way of getting involved in the macro environment.

questions.question: Building useful contacts and relationships to help cope with the business environment is called _________.
questions.memo: Networking is building contacts and relationships — for example to find new customers or partners.

questions.question: True or false: A takeover (acquisition) is when one business buys another business.
questions.memo: In a takeover or acquisition, one business buys another and takes control of it.

questions.question: Cooperating with another business while each stays separate is called forming a _________ alliance.
questions.memo: A strategic alliance is an agreement where two businesses cooperate for mutual benefit while remaining separate companies.

questions.question: Sort each way of adapting into the right group.

items.text: Lobbying the government for fair rules
Cross-training staff so they can switch roles

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Mergers and takeovers combine firms; lobbying and networking influence outsiders; reorganising and cross-training build internal flexibility.

questions.question: A business merges with a competitor to cope with tough competition. This adaptation is best described as a:
questions.memo: Merging with a competitor is a strategic response to market pressure — combining strengths to compete better.

questions.question: _________ management means gathering and using information about the environment so the business can make better decisions.
questions.memo: Information management is collecting and using reliable information about the environment to respond well to change.

questions.question: Why might a business form a strategic alliance with another firm?
options: To gain strength to cope with an environment it cannot control
questions.expected: To gain strength to cope with an environment it cannot control
questions.memo: Alliances pool strengths and contacts so each business is better able to cope with pressures it cannot face alone.

questions.question: True or false: Acting with social responsibility can be a way for a business to respond positively to its environment.
questions.memo: Social responsibility — giving back to the community and protecting the environment — is one recognised way a business responds to its environment and builds goodwill.

questions.question: Thesis: 'A small business should network actively to help it cope with its business environment.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: A small business should network actively to help it cope with its business environment.

pool.text: Networking can bring in new customers and suppliers
Contacts can share useful information about coming changes
Partnerships built through networking can open new opportunities
Networking lets the business control the whole economy
The owner enjoys free snacks at networking events
Networking is only worth doing once the business is already huge

questions.memo: The strong reasons are new customers/suppliers, early information, and new opportunities. The others overclaim, are irrelevant, or wrongly limit networking to big businesses.

questions.question: A firm redesigns its structure so it can react faster when the market changes. This is an example of:
questions.memo: Changing the structure to respond quickly is organisation design and flexibility — building the ability to adapt into the business itself.

questions.question: Sort each action into the type of involvement it shows.

items.text: Petitioning regulators to change a proposed rule
Meeting potential clients at a trade fair
Forming a strategic alliance with a major firm
Bargaining with government over an industry law
Swapping contacts with other small business owners
Persuading large investors to back the business

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Lobbying influences rule-makers; networking builds contacts; power relationships use alliances and big investors to gain strength.

questions.question: What is the difference between a merger and a takeover?
options: A merger combines two firms into one; a takeover is one firm buying another
A merger is illegal; a takeover is legal
A merger only happens between small firms
There is no difference between them
questions.expected: A merger combines two firms into one; a takeover is one firm buying another
questions.memo: In a merger both firms join as equals into one business; in a takeover one firm buys and controls the other.

questions.question: Persuading large investors to back the business and forming alliances are examples of using _________ relationships.
questions.memo: Power relationships use strategic alliances and the influence of large investors to give the business more strength in its environment.

questions.question: A rise in fuel prices (a macro factor) has pushed up a delivery firm's costs. Which response shows it adapting sensibly?
options: Planning more efficient routes and reviewing its prices
Demanding that fuel prices be lowered for it alone
questions.expected: Planning more efficient routes and reviewing its prices
questions.memo: It cannot control fuel prices, so it adapts — cutting fuel use through better routes and adjusting prices to stay viable.

questions.question: Two firms agree to share a distribution network while staying fully independent companies. This is best described as:
questions.memo: Cooperating for mutual benefit while remaining separate companies is a strategic alliance — not a merger (one firm) or takeover (one buys the other).

questions.question: Evaluate: 'A business facing a macro challenge can only sit back and suffer.' Which response is best?
options: Incorrect — it can adapt, manage information, build flexibility, and lobby or network
Correct — there is nothing any business can ever do
Incorrect — it can simply control the macro environment
questions.expected: Incorrect — it can adapt, manage information, build flexibility, and lobby or network
questions.memo: A business cannot control the macro environment but has many active responses: adapting, gathering information, staying flexible, and lobbying or networking.

questions.question: A struggling business buys out the supplier it depends on so it can secure its raw materials. This adaptation is a:
questions.memo: Buying out another business — here a supplier — is a takeover or acquisition, used as a strategic response to secure supply.
